title: System Overlay
concept: A five-step order for hard conversations, so they end somewhere: you both start warm and safe, one of you says what happened and asks for one thing, and you leave knowing who does what.
whenToUse: Any sensitive conversation, request for change, repair, or decision you’re making together. Going in circles? Find the step you skipped and go back to it.
steps: Warm up — say the warmest true thing you can. Remind each other you’re on the same team.
Make it safe — say out loud that the relationship isn’t at risk tonight.
Say what happened — what happened, how it felt, what it meant.
Ask for one thing — specific, doable, with a timeframe.
Agree on next steps — who does what, by when, and when you’ll check back in.

phrases.text: I love us, and I’m not trying to fight.
When X happened, I felt Y; the impact was Z.
Can we try ___ this week and check in on ___?

working: B opens warm, says it isn’t a breakup talk, then: “When you scrolled while I talked, I felt dismissed and shut down.” One ask: ten phone-free minutes at night. They try it for a week and check in on Friday.
notWorking: Jumping straight to a rule: “No phones at night — it’s rude.” Without warming up, making it safe, and owning your side first, it comes across as control, and the fight turns into “always/never.”
activity: A 12-minute practice run: pick something low-stakes, use all five steps out loud, and the listener keeps you to the order. Aim for a little better, not perfect.
